# .NET secure coding

- Use ASP.NET Core/framework binding with dedicated request models and validation. Do not bind request data directly to entities containing ownership, role, price, or administrative fields.
- Use EF LINQ or parameterized `DbCommand`/`SqlCommand`. Never concatenate input into SQL, stored-procedure text, dynamic LINQ, LDAP filters, or sort/column names.
- Do not use `BinaryFormatter`, `LosFormatter`, `SoapFormatter`, `NetDataContractSerializer`, or type-enabled JSON deserialization with untrusted data. Prefer `System.Text.Json` DTOs with constrained polymorphism.
- Start processes without a shell, using a fixed executable and `ArgumentList`. Do not concatenate untrusted input into `cmd.exe`, PowerShell, or a command string.
- Configure XML readers with DTD processing prohibited and no external resolver. Apply document size/depth limits.
- Preserve Razor encoding; do not pass untrusted content to `Html.Raw`, dynamically constructed templates, or JavaScript contexts. Sanitize intentional rich HTML with a maintained allowlist sanitizer.
- Use ASP.NET Core Data Protection for protected application tokens and the platform cryptography APIs for primitives. Keep keys outside source and share/protect the key ring correctly in multi-instance deployments.
- Require authorization policies/resource handlers for protected controllers, minimal APIs, hubs, and background operations. Do not rely only on `[Authorize]` when object-level checks are needed.
- Use secure cookie defaults and antiforgery for cookie-authenticated state changes. Validate forwarded headers only from configured trusted proxies.
- Propagate `CancellationToken`, cap request/body/upload sizes, and avoid unbounded async fan-out or blocking on async work.
- Prefer safe paths with `Path.GetFullPath` plus a verified base directory and generated storage names. Do not trust `IFormFile.FileName`.
- Keep nullable-reference analysis and security analyzers enabled; do not suppress warnings broadly or expose developer exception pages outside development.
- For legacy ASP.NET, never disable ViewState MAC/event validation; protect and rotate machine keys consistently across the deployment. Prefer migration away from unsafe legacy serializers and ViewState patterns.
